dummyBot.title: In-game Bot
dummyBot.conversationDescription: Read-only mirror. Send commands to {{name}} in the Riot or VALORANT client.
dummyBot.translateDesc: Whisper this to the bot. Only the translation is sent to that room. Language can be a name or code: french, de, ko, ko-KR, ja-JP, zh_tw, zh-TW. Use auto for the Settings language, or none to send it untranslated.
dummyBot.historyDesc: Whisper this to the bot. Reads the last n party/team/all lines and whispers the translations back to you. Optional channel: /tran team 5.
dummyBot.asciiDesc: Without a channel the artwork is private: it comes back to you as a Dummy Bot message. Name party, team or all to post it. Draws A-Z, digits and ! ? - as block letters: a bold font for up to 5 characters per line (2 lines), or a compact font for up to 6 per line (3 lines). Text only breaks between words. The panel is at most 13 rows (350 characters, the chat limit).
dummyBot.aiDesc: Asks your AI provider (Settings → AI) to write one chat line. By default only you get it, as a Dummy Bot DM or under the Chat composer. Name a channel to post it to that room instead. Whisper it to the bot or type it in the Chat composer; typed in party/pregame/team/all chat it does not run, and the bot whispers you a reminder. Slow models can take up to a minute.
dummyBot.aiExample: /ai team hype us up for overtime
dummyBot.askDesc: Asks your AI provider a question. Only you get the answer, as a Dummy Bot DM or under the Chat composer. Whisper it to the bot or type it in the Chat composer; typed in party/pregame/team/all chat it does not run, and the bot whispers you a reminder.
dummyBot.askExample: /ask how do I retake B on Ascent?
dummyBot.prefixNote: Chat commands start with / (for example, /party leave); . works too. When you whisper the bot, no prefix is needed: who, tran 3, help rr.
dummyBot.whoDesc: Lists everyone in agent select or the match: Riot ID (unless they hid it outside your party), agent, rank and RR, peak, party and recent form. Uses the Live Game roster, so it adds no Riot requests. Works whispered to the bot, in the Chat composer, and typed in party/pregame/team/all chat, where your line is hidden and the answer is whispered only to you.
dummyBot.rrDesc: Your rank and RR, peak, this act's record and the RR from your recent competitive games. Uses your saved Career data and refreshes it only when it is out of date. Works anywhere /who does; only you see the answer.
dummyBot.helpDesc: Lists every command, or explains one with its syntax and an example: /help tran. Works anywhere /who does; only you see the answer.
dummyBot.metDesc: Lists players in agent select or the match who were in your last 10 matches, with how often they were with or against you and when. Uses the cached Played before data. Works anywhere /who does; only you see the answer.
dummyBot.lastDesc: Your last match: result, score, map, mode, agent, K/D/A, ACS, headshot rate and RR change. Works anywhere /who does; only you see the answer. A saved custom command named /who, /rr or /last keeps working and takes priority.
dummyBot.partyJoinDesc: Join a party using its invite code, for example /party join TUE693. Double quotes around the code are optional.
dummyBot.codeCreateDesc: Generate an invite code for your current party. The code is shown only to you.
dummyBot.dodgeDesc: Leave agent select. Whisper this to the bot or type it in the Chat composer. Typed in party/pregame/team/all chat it does not dodge, and the bot whispers you a reminder.
dummyBot.customDesc: Create typed commands or automatic match events. Send can post to a room or whisper you through Dummy Bot; Translate history reads recent group chat.

apiReference.subtitle: Riot Client REST API
apiReference.description: Hosts the running Riot Client's OpenAPI spec on a local port and opens it as a browsable API reference. The spec is read live, so it always matches your installed client version.

apiReference.aboutBody: The Riot Client is built from plugins, and each one registers its own endpoints on the local HTTP server — roughly 790 paths across 96 groups. Most are undocumented internals that Riot can change or remove in any patch. ValoUtils itself uses only a handful of them.

mcpDocs.title: MCP docs
mcpDocs.subtitle: Connect AI agents to ValoUtils and see what they can do.
mcpDocs.intro: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI agents use tools. ValoUtils runs a small MCP server on this PC so your agent can read your Valorant data and open the game.
mcpDocs.step1: In Settings → AI agents (MCP), turn on “Let AI agents use ValoUtils”.
mcpDocs.step2: Copy the setup for your agent (Claude Code command, Claude Desktop JSON, HTTP-client JSON) or paste the agent prompt.
mcpDocs.step3: Ask your agent about your Valorant account. It calls the tools below when it needs data.
mcpDocs.off: The MCP server is off. Turn it on in Settings.
mcpDocs.clients: Works with any MCP client: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and others. Web chat apps can't reach it, because it only listens on this PC.

mcpDocs.privacyLocal: Only reachable from this PC (127.0.0.1), and every request needs your secret token. Web pages can't connect.
mcpDocs.privacyNames: Live match and scoreboard tools label other players You / Ally N / Enemy N, never by name. Friends and Look up a player do return Riot IDs, because that's what they're for.
mcpDocs.privacyRate: Agent calls share Riot's request budget with the app. If Riot rate-limits, the tool tells the agent when to try again.
